morphology_entries.coding_note: Generated by build/generate_group11_entries.py from ICCC-2017.sqlite joined to icdo32.sqlite (build_inventory, group XI), never transcribed from the REDCap option file (contract §2). ICD-O-3.2 preferred term at /3 is 'Carcinoma, NOS'. Carcinoma of the adrenal gland whose cortical origin the reports do not show (SF1 negative, not done or not reported), at basis 7, and a carcinoma that cytology names without its type, at basis 5. No ICCC-2017 range holds 8010 at C74; standing rule 3 keeps it in Group XI with the default subgroup XIf10 (registrar question 5). Carcinoma whose type the report does not name: basis 7 on the histology screen and as the stain panel's fallback, basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type, and the nearest generic code for a high-grade differentiated thyroid carcinoma whose dominant type the report does not name (D4, registrar question 6). Nasopharyngeal carcinoma whose type the report does not state and does not call squamous, on the type screen (registrar review A3, Q18: 8010/3 or 8070/3); at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type. Salivary gland carcinoma whose type the report does not name: basis 7 on the histology screen, basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type or a type the cytology screen does not list. Carcinoma whose type the report does not name: the generic option of the colorectal and appendix histology screens (contract §4.2), and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type. Carcinoma of the lung whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type or a type the cytology list does not hold. Carcinoma of the thymus or mediastinum whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type or a type the cytology list does not hold. Carcinoma whose type the report does not name: basis 7 on the skin histology screen, basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type. Breast carcinoma whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen, and any carcinoma cytology names at the breast, at basis 5: the type is not settled on a limited sample (ICCR Invasive Breast 2022, p. 12). Carcinoma whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the female genital histology screen and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type. Carcinoma whose type the report does not name, and urachal carcinoma with no subtype named (Netto 2022 Table 3), on the urinary and male genital histology screen; at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type or a type the cytology screen does not show. Carcinoma of the eye, lacrimal gland or orbit whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen, and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma only. No source reports an eye carcinoma in children (Pfister 2022 Table 3; Milman 2023), so every named carcinoma type is a picker entry. Carcinoma of the head and neck whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen (ICCR-Nasal p. 7), and at basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type. Carcinoma whose type the report does not name: basis 5 when cytology names a carcinoma without its type or a type the cytology screen does not show, the pancreas stain panel's fallback, and in the digestive picker. Carcinoma of the pleura, heart or another thoracic or respiratory site whose type the report does not name, at basis 7 on the histology screen, and at basis 5 at C80.9 when pleural or pericardial fluid cytology shows a carcinoma and the file does not name the organ where it began. No primary carcinoma of these sites is reported (evidence data gap 5). Carcinoma whose type the cytology report does not name, at basis 5 on the cytology screen. Carcinoma whose type the report does not name: basis 7 on the histology screen (at C80.9 when the deposit question sends a carcinoma with no primary found here), and basis 5 on the cytology screen. ICCC-2017 range 136 places 8010/3 at C80.9 in XIf11. ICD-O-3.2 preferred term at /3 is 'Adenocarcinoma, NOS'. Salivary gland carcinoma, not otherwise specified, or adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified (the International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting salivary gland dataset, Table 1, codes the category 8140/3), on the salivary histology screen and at basis 5 from cytology. Adenocarcinoma with no subtype named: a paediatric option on the colorectal histology screen (Polat 2021, Mahajan 2022), the generic adenocarcinoma option of the appendix screen (contract §4.2), and at basis 5 when cytology names it. Adenocarcinoma of the lung with no subtype named (Ozkan 2024) on the histology screen and at basis 5 from cytology; a non-small cell carcinoma favouring adenocarcinoma, in words or by TTF-1 or a mucin stain, that the file confirms (SEER lung rule H3; Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 5); and acinar adenocarcinoma, whose code 8551/3 carries an obsolete Preferred term and is held off every screen until the registrar rules (D3). Adenocarcinoma, NOS as the thymus stain panel's fallback when no intestinal marker is positive (Marx 2022, p. 7), and in the thymus picker. Adenocarcinoma with no type named on the female genital histology screen (Wohlmuth 2021: cervix and uterus at ages 0 to 18), including an adenocarcinoma called HPV-associated or HPV-independent with no other type (8483 and 8484 are not ICD-O-3.2 codes; registrar question 1) and a mesonephric-like adenocarcinoma (9113 is not an ICD-O-3.2 code; registrar question 2); at basis 5 when cytology names an adenocarcinoma; in the picker for Carcinoma of Skene, Cowper and Littre glands. Adenocarcinoma with no type named, mixed adenocarcinoma (the ICCR prints 8140/3; registrar question 4), carcinoma of the Littre, Skene or Cowper glands and acinar adenocarcinoma of the prostate on the urinary and male genital histology screen; at basis 5 when cytology names an adenocarcinoma. Adenocarcinoma named on eye cytology, at basis 5 (Milman 2023, PDF pp. 10 and 12); a histology report reaches it from the picker. Adenocarcinoma of the nose or sinuses with no type named, or non-intestinal-type adenocarcinoma (ICCR-Nasal p. 8), and the minor salivary gland adenocarcinoma with no type named (Rules p. 11). Adenocarcinoma at basis 5 when cytology of a digestive organ names it, and in the digestive picker. Parathyroid carcinoma on the histology screen at basis 7, and at basis 5 when cytology of a deposit away from the gland calls it metastatic parathyroid carcinoma; the case is recorded at C75.0. ICD-O-3.2 lists Parathyroid carcinoma as a related term of Adenocarcinoma, NOS (ICCR Table 1 prints 8140/3). Rare in children: Pfister 2022 Table 3 lists parathyroid endocrine tumours without naming carcinoma (registrar question 1). Adenocarcinoma with no primary site found, named by cytology, at basis 5 and C80.9. nodes.question: What is in the file for this adrenal tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. Hormone results (cortisol, androgens, aldosterone, adrenocorticotropic hormone) do not change the code and register no code without tissue. A neuroblastoma or phaeochromocytoma diagnosed from imaging and biochemical results is coded from the Group IV tree, which has its own route for it: go back and choose Group IV (neuroblastoma and other peripheral nervous cell tumours).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence ac_evidence (departure 1).

A Weiss score is a different system, used for adults: answer No for it. When the report states a behaviour (benign, malignant or uncertain malignant potential) that differs from its score, answer No and choose the stated behaviour.

A report that says papillary and follicular carcinoma is the infiltrative follicular variant (8340).

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the report states it.
nodes.hint: The histology report calls the tumour a carcinoma without naming its type. Answer 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. Thyroglobulin, TTF-1 and PAX8 show that a tumour comes from follicular cells; they do not name its type.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence th_ihc and ihc_rules (departure 11). Fallback 8010/3: ICCR p. 19 'Thyroglobulin, thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) and PAX8 may indicate'. Mucoepidermoid carcinoma has no rule: Juhlin p. 7 gives p63 and CK5 as confirming stains and no marker that separates it (evidence §4).

resolution_logic.reason: Calcitonin is positive and thyroglobulin is not: the medullary thyroid carcinoma pattern (Juhlin 2022, p. 7; ICCR thyroid dataset, p. 19). Recorded as Medullary thyroid carcinoma (8345/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Evidence ihc_rules 1. ICCR p. 19 'calcitonin, chromogranin, synaptophysin, carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and thyroglobulin may be performed' and 'Thyroglobulin, thyroid transcription factor-1 (TTF-1) and PAX8 may indicate'; Juhlin p. 7 'verified by calcitonin immunohistochemistry'.

resolution_logic.reason: Nuclear beta-catenin is positive and thyroglobulin is not: the cribriform-morular thyroid carcinoma pattern (Juhlin 2022, p. 7). Recorded as Cribriform carcinoma, NOS (8201/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Evidence ihc_rules 2. Juhlin p. 7 'presence of nuclear and cytoplasmic beta-catenin expression' and 'these tumors lack expression of thyroglobulin'. ICCR Table 1 (p. 9, image) codes the entity 8201/3.

resolution_logic.reason: GATA3, mammaglobin and S100 protein are positive, and TTF-1 and thyroglobulin are not: the secretory carcinoma pattern (Juhlin 2022, p. 7). Recorded as Secretory carcinoma (8502/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Evidence ihc_rules 3. Juhlin p. 7 'positive for GATA3, mammaglobin, GCDFP15 and S100 protein' and 'consistently negative for TTF1 and thyroglobulin'. D11: no ICCC-2017 range holds 8502 at C73.9.

nos_fallback.name: Carcinoma, NOS
nos_fallback.reason: The stains do not establish the carcinoma's type. Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3). Thyroglobulin, TTF-1 and PAX8 show that a tumour comes from follicular cells; they do not name its type (ICCR thyroid dataset, p. 19).

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the thyroid are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. The six exclusions and the nodular disease line of evidence th_histology (departure 5).

nodes.question: What is in the file for this salivary gland tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A fine-needle aspiration report counts as cytology. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A cytology or biopsy report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A tumour of a minor salivary gland, in the palate, lip, cheek, tongue or another part of the mouth or a neighbouring organ, is not coded to these glands: go back to the site step and record the place where the gland lies, or mouth, not otherwise specified (C06.9), when the report names none. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence sg_document_inventory and sg_cytology (departures 3 to 6). No laboratory screen and no marker tier: Visser 2023 Table 4 names no salivary marker (evidence §§5-6).

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the salivary glands in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.question: What does the cytology report conclude?
nodes.hint: Use the cytology report's own conclusion. Cytology gives basis of diagnosis 5; a histology report gives the full type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D8: cytology naming an entity codes it at basis 5 (Visser 2023 Table 1, p. 03); malignant cells with no type refer to Group XII with 8001; suspicious is not registrable (rule 4).

options.reason: Recorded as Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8430/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1, built per named type (departure 6).

options.label: Acinic cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Acinar cell carcinoma (8550/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. ICD-O-3.2 gives Acinic cell adenocarcinoma as a synonym of this code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1 (departure 6).

options.label: Secretory carcinoma, or microsecretory adenocarcinoma

options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1 (departures 6 and 8).

options.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Adenoid cystic carcinoma (8200/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1 (departure 6).

options.label: Polymorphous adenocarcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Polymorphous adenocarcinoma (8525/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. ICD-O-3.2 gives Polymorphous carcinoma as a synonym of this code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1 (departure 6).

options.label: Salivary gland carcinoma, not otherwise specified, or adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified
options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 1 (departure 6).

options.label: Cytology names a carcinoma of a type not listed above, or a carcinoma without naming its type
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. A type this screen does not list is recorded as the carcinoma code; the histology report gives the type its own code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence sg_cytology option 2, widened to the types the screen does not list (departure 6; request 1: a cytology picker).

options.label: Myoepithelial carcinoma, carcinosarcoma or malignant mixed tumour
options.reason: ICCC-3 codes Myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3), Carcinosarcoma, NOS (8980/3) and Mixed tumor, malignant, NOS (8940/3) in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms, subgroup XIIa4), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Departure 6: not in the evidence's cytology screen; added so a cytology report naming one of these records no Group XI code.

options.label: Lymphoma
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the salivary glands keeps the salivary glands as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. The hop carries the case's site.

options.label: Malignant cells are present, with no tumour type named
options.reason: Cytology establishes malignant cells but no tumour type. It is registered as Tumor cells, malignant (8001/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. ICCC-3 places that code at the salivary glands in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves imaging as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and no imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology and no imaging leave the note as the best evidence; Cytology stays on the case (Group 10's split).

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. The grade the report gives, and high grade transformation, do not change the code: choose the carcinoma type the report names. A carcinoma ex pleomorphic adenoma is recorded as such whatever carcinoma the report names inside it. When the report names two carcinoma types in one tumour and no option names both, choose the one with the higher ICD-O code (WHO coding Rule K). Myoepithelial carcinoma, carcinosarcoma and malignant mixed tumour are coded in Group XII: their options are at the end of the list.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence sg_histology (departures 2 and 7 to 15). D1: the paediatric entities are mucoepidermoid, acinic cell and secretory carcinoma (Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5; Pfister 2022, p. 14), and adenoid cystic carcinoma and polymorphous adenocarcinoma (Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5, observed less often in children). Intraductal carcinoma is an option because its code needs the invasion answer.

options.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8430/3).
options.coding_note: D1: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5.
options.recognition_aid: The report may give a low, intermediate or high grade, or name a CRTC1::MAML2 or CRTC3::MAML2 fusion.

options.label: Acinic cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Acinar cell carcinoma (8550/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Acinic cell adenocarcinoma as a synonym of this code.
options.coding_note: D1: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5; Pfister 2022, p. 14. Evidence code_currency 8550: the WHO name is not an ICD-O-3.2 term.
options.recognition_aid: The report may name an NR4A3 rearrangement, or high grade transformation.

options.label: Secretory carcinoma, or microsecretory adenocarcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Secretory carcinoma (8502/3). The World Health Organization classification codes microsecretory adenocarcinoma 8502/3 (International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting, salivary gland dataset, Table 1).
options.coding_note: D1: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5. Departure 8: the evidence's microsecretory picker option merges here.
options.recognition_aid: Secretory carcinoma resembles acinic cell carcinoma. The report may name an ETV6 translocation, an ETV6::NTRK3 fusion or strong mammaglobin staining. Microsecretory adenocarcinoma carries an MEF2C::SS18 fusion.

options.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Adenoid cystic carcinoma (8200/3).
options.coding_note: D1: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5 (evidence data gap 2: no paediatric count).
options.recognition_aid: The report may describe a tubular, cribriform or solid pattern, or name a MYB::NFIB fusion or another MYB or MYBL1 rearrangement.

options.label: Polymorphous adenocarcinoma, classic or cribriform subtype
options.reason: Recorded as Polymorphous adenocarcinoma (8525/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Polymorphous carcinoma as a synonym of this code.
options.coding_note: D1: Perez-de-Oliveira 2025 §5 (evidence data gap 2).
options.recognition_aid: Cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland origin is the cribriform subtype of polymorphous adenocarcinoma. Older reports call it polymorphous low-grade adenocarcinoma.

options.label: Salivary duct carcinoma, or intraductal carcinoma
options.coding_note: D1 exception (invasion screen); departure 9.
options.recognition_aid: An intraductal carcinoma keeps an intact layer of myoepithelial cells around its ducts; a report of invasive growth describes loss of that layer.

options.label: Salivary gland carcinoma, not otherwise specified, or adenocarcinoma, not otherwise specified
options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3).
options.upgrade_path: The report does not state the tumour's type. A report that names it gives that type's own code: go back and take the option that names it.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_histology option 7; the generic option of the screen (evidence data gap 7).

options.label: Carcinoma, with no type named
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3).
options.upgrade_path: The report does not state the tumour's type. A report that names it gives that type's own code: go back and take the option that names it.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_histology option 8; the generic option of the screen (evidence data gap 7).

options.label: The report places the tumour beside a salivary gland or in its region (for example periparotid), not in the gland
options.coding_note: Departure 2: the Rule B option of evidence sg_site; registrar question 9.

options.label: Sialoblastoma
options.reason: Sialoblastoma is a malignant tumour of the salivary glands in infants and young children (the WHO classification of paediatric tumours). ICCC-3 places sialoblastoma (8974) at behaviour 3 in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree, as malignant.
options.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A11, E10). ICD-O-3.2 prints 8974 at /1 only; 8974/3 is Group XII's to record (TODO §35.12).

options.label: Melanoma
options.coding_note: D13: cross-tree next_node into the melanoma tree (me_mucosa), which offers every XId code. group11_tree.trees() defers this hop while g11_melanoma has no module.

options.label: NUT carcinoma (also written NUT midline carcinoma, BRD4::NUTM1 carcinoma or carcinoma with t(15;19) translocation), or a carcinoma reported with a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene result
options.coding_note: D12: NUT carcinoma evidence (NUT_carcinoma.json, nut_site_option).
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe a poorly differentiated or undifferentiated carcinoma, sometimes with abrupt keratinization, and nuclear staining for NUT.

options.label: Another carcinoma the report names - type its name to find it
options.coding_note: D2: the Group XI picker.
options.recognition_aid: ICD-O-3.2 lists hyalinizing clear cell carcinoma as Clear cell adenocarcinoma, NOS, and sclerosing microcystic adenocarcinoma as Microcystic adnexal carcinoma: type those names.

options.label: A tumour the report calls benign, borderline or in situ, such as pleomorphic adenoma, Warthin tumour, another adenoma, myoepithelioma or oncocytoma
options.coding_note: The exclusion screen (contract §4.2).

options.label: A deposit of a tumour that began elsewhere
options.recognition_aid: A squamous cell carcinoma in a salivary gland is typically a deposit from a primary in the skin or mucosa, often in a lymph node within or beside the gland.

options.label: Malignant tumour, type not determined by the report
options.reason: The report establishes a malignant tumour without determining its type. It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3). ICCC-3 places that code at the salivary glands in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Lymphoma of the salivary gland itself
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the salivary glands keeps the salivary glands as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. The hop carries the case's site.

options.label: Lymphoma in a lymph node within or beside a salivary gland (an intraparotid, periparotid or submandibular lymph node)
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma in a lymph node within or beside a salivary gland is a lymph node lymphoma, coded to the lymph node and not to the gland (WHO Rule D). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree at the lymph node's site.
options.coding_note: Departure 13. ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. recapture_site: the gland is not the lymphoma's site.

options.label: Leukaemia, or leukaemic infiltration
options.reason: Leukaemic infiltration of the salivary glands is coded as the leukaemia, in ICCC-3 Group I, and a leukaemia is recorded at the bone marrow (C42.1). Code the case from the Group I (leukaemias) tree.
options.coding_note: WHO Rule E (section 4.2.8): every leukaemia except myeloid sarcoma is C42.1, so the hop carries the marrow. A myeloid sarcoma option is not built: check_leukaemia_referrals_record_marrow admits a site-keeping Group I referral only on the nodes it lists.

options.label: Rhabdomyosarcoma or another sarcoma
options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the salivary glands belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 places 8800-8921 and 9120-9133 in Group IX at the Group XI sites; a bone sarcoma arises in bone, which no Group XI tree routes.

options.label: Teratoma or another germ cell tumour
options.reason: Germ cell tumours, teratomas among them, belong to ICCC-3 Group X at the salivary glands. Code the case from the Group X (germ cell tumours) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 range 101 (Xb2) places 9080-9084 at the extragonadal sites.

options.label: Another malignant tumour the report names that is not a carcinoma or melanoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 Group XII holds the specified malignant tumours no other group codes. Code the case from the Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) tree.

options.label: Myoepithelial carcinoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 codes Myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3) in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms, subgroup XIIa4), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_carcinoma_picker option 17; registrar question 2. ICCC-2017 code_lookup 8982 XII XIIa4 000-809.

options.label: Carcinosarcoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 codes Carcinosarcoma, NOS (8980/3) in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms, subgroup XIIa4), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_carcinoma_picker option 18; registrar question 2. ICCC-2017 code_lookup 8980 XII XIIa4 000-809.

options.label: Malignant mixed tumour
options.reason: ICCC-3 codes Mixed tumor, malignant, NOS (8940/3) in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms, subgroup XIIa4), not in Group XI. ICD-O-3.2 gives Mixed tumor, salivary gland type, malignant as a synonym of this code. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_carcinoma_picker option 19. ICCC-2017 code_lookup 8940 XII XIIa4 000-809. Not a WHO 5th-edition entity; ICD-O-3.2 keeps it current.

nodes.question: Which duct carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: An intraductal carcinoma is in situ while its layer of myoepithelial cells is intact. It is coded as invasive only when the report states invasion or invasive growth (WHO coding Rule F).
nodes.coding_note: Departure 9. D1 exception: intraductal carcinoma's code depends on invasion. ICD-O-3.2 prints no salivary duct carcinoma term; the WHO code is 8500/3 (evidence code_currency 8500).

options.label: Salivary duct carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS (8500/3). The World Health Organization classification codes salivary duct carcinoma 8500/3 (International Collaboration on Cancer Reporting, salivary gland dataset, Table 1). ICD-O links this code to the breast, but the salivary gland stays the site (WHO coding Rule H).
options.coding_note: Departure 9: the evidence's picker option.

options.label: Intraductal carcinoma, and the report states invasion or invasive growth
options.reason: Recorded as Infiltrating duct carcinoma, NOS (8500/3). The report states invasion, so the invasive code is recorded (WHO coding Rule F). This awaits the registrar's decision.
options.coding_note: Evidence sg_not_malignant option 9; registrar question 3.

options.label: Intraductal carcinoma, with no invasion stated

behaviour_exclusion.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes an intraductal carcinoma with no invasion stated as Intraductal carcinoma, noninfiltrating, NOS (8500/2), behaviour 2, in situ. ICD-O-3.2 gives Intraductal carcinoma, NOS as a synonym of this code. ICCC-3 Group XI registers behaviour 3 (malignant) only, so no Group XI code is recorded.

options.coding_note: Evidence sg_not_malignant option 8. ICCR p. 8 image 'Intraductal carcinoma 8500/2'.

nodes.question: Does the tumour's type show that it arose in the salivary gland?
nodes.hint: The report places the tumour beside the gland or in its region (for example periparotid, or in the region of the parotid), not in it. Such a tumour is coded to the gland only when its type shows that it arose there; otherwise it is coded to head, face or neck, not otherwise specified (C76.0) (WHO coding Rule B).
nodes.coding_note: Departure 2: the Rule B option of evidence sg_site (registrar question 9). The router answers the gland itself (D14).

options.label: Yes: the report names a salivary gland carcinoma type, for example mucoepidermoid, acinic cell, secretory, adenoid cystic or polymorphous carcinoma, or calls it a salivary gland carcinoma
options.coding_note: Rule B exception: the type indicates origin in the gland, so the routed site stands. Returns to the histology screen, as nut_tests returns.

options.label: No: a carcinoma of another type, such as squamous cell carcinoma, or a carcinoma whose type the report does not name
options.coding_note: Rule B: C76.0, then the unspecified tree's histology screen (cross-tree next_node), the deposit node's pattern for C80.9. ICCC-2017 range 136 places the shared list at C76.0 in XIf11. group11_tree.trees() defers this hop while g11_unspecified has no module.

nodes.question: What does the file report for this tumour?
nodes.hint: Choose the first answer that matches the file. Keratin, p63, p40 and CD99 stains do not decide NUT carcinoma; a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene test does.
nodes.coding_note: D12. NUT_carcinoma.json nut_result. Lemelle 2022, p. 7 ('This epithelial epidermoid marker is nonspecific in this setting'; 'falsely suggested by tumour expression of CD99'); Luo 2025, p. 6-7.

options.label: The sample is a deposit in a lymph node, bone, liver or another organ, and the file names a different site where the tumour began
options.coding_note: NUT evidence nut_result: Luo 2025, p. 8 ('Common sites of metastasis of NUT carcinoma include bone and liver'); Lemelle 2022, p. 6. D10: the deposit question asks the primary.

options.label: The report calls the tumour a sarcoma with a NUTM1 rearrangement (for example undifferentiated epithelioid sarcoma with CIC, BCORL1 or MXD1), and it arises in a bone
options.reason: A NUTM1-rearranged sarcoma is not NUT carcinoma. It is coded with the malignant bone tumours (Group VIII) at the bone it arises in.
options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 2 ('other NUTM1 fusion partners (that is, CIC, MXD4 and YAP1) are typically WHO-unclassified sarcomas') and p. 5. recapture_site: the bone is not this tree's site.

options.label: The report calls the tumour a sarcoma with a NUTM1 rearrangement, at any site other than bone
options.reason: A NUTM1-rearranged sarcoma is not NUT carcinoma. It is coded with the soft-tissue and other extraosseous sarcomas (Group IX).
options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 2 and p. 5 ('most often in the abdomen, soft tissue or central nervous system').

options.label: The report calls the tumour a leukaemia with a NUTM1 rearrangement
options.reason: A NUTM1-rearranged leukaemia is not NUT carcinoma. It is coded with the leukaemias (Group I) and recorded at the bone marrow (C42.1).
options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 13 and p. 5 (table image); WHO Rule E, p. 15.

options.label: The diagnosis names NUT carcinoma or NUT midline carcinoma
options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 2; Lemelle 2022, p. 4.

options.label: The diagnosis names another carcinoma (for example poorly differentiated carcinoma), and the file reports a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene test
options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 7 ('In the context of a tumour with a carcinoma histology'; 'diffuse (>50% of nuclei) positive for nuclear staining by NUT IHC is 100% specific'); Lemelle 2022, p. 6.

nodes.question: Does the file hold a positive NUTM1 gene result?
nodes.hint: A NUTM1 result is written as a NUTM1 (NUT) rearrangement, a translocation t(15;19), or a fusion such as BRD4::NUTM1, BRD3::NUTM1 or NSD3::NUTM1, found by FISH, RT-PCR or sequencing.
nodes.coding_note: D12. NUT_carcinoma.json nut_basis. D5: NUT carcinoma with squamous features is 8023/3, the entity's one code.

options.label: Yes: a NUTM1 rearrangement or fusion is reported
options.reason: Recorded as Nuclear protein in testis (NUT)-associated carcinoma (8023/3). Squamous features named in the same report do not change the code.
options.coding_note: D12, D15 (a gene test specific to the entity, basis 8). Lemelle 2022, p. 7 ('the translocation involving BRD3/4 and NUT is specific for NC'), p. 2; Luo 2025, p. 2, p. 6.

options.label: No: the diagnosis rests on the histology report, with or without a NUT immunostain
options.reason: Recorded as Nuclear protein in testis (NUT)-associated carcinoma (8023/3). Squamous features named in the same report do not change the code.
options.coding_note: D12. Lemelle 2022, p. 2 ('The diagnosis is guided by anti-NUT nuclear immunostaining'), p. 6; Luo 2025, p. 2, p. 6.

nodes.question: Which NUT results does the file report?
nodes.hint: Choose the first answer that matches. A NUT immunostain counts only when the report states nuclear staining in more than half (over 50%) of the tumour cells.
nodes.coding_note: D12. NUT_carcinoma.json nut_ihc, built as a choice (see nut_nodes()).

options.label: A NUTM1 rearrangement or fusion found by FISH, RT-PCR or sequencing
options.reason: Recorded as Nuclear protein in testis (NUT)-associated carcinoma (8023/3). Squamous features named in the same report do not change the code.
options.coding_note: D12, D15. NUT evidence ihc_rules order 1: Luo 2025, p. 2; Lemelle 2022, p. 6, p. 7.

options.label: A NUT immunostain with nuclear staining in more than half (over 50%) of the tumour cells

decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the colon and rectum (C18.0, C18.2-C21.8; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the colon, rectum or anus?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A tumour reported only in the tissue beside the bowel, such as retrocaecal tissue, is not a tumour of the bowel: ICD-O-3.1 lists that tissue under the retroperitoneum (C48.0), so go back to the site step. One tumour that spans two parts of the colon is recorded at C18.8, and one that spans the rectum, anus and anal canal at C21.8 (WHO coding Rule C). A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence dg_document_inventory, dg_marker and dg_cytology (departures 2 to 4 in the module docstring).

options.coding_note: D7. Visser O, et al. Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, Table 4, p. 06, read from the page image (contract §0.5), with rule 6, p. 05 (basis 4 never stands alone). Neuroendocrine tumour, chromogranin A; the row names no site. Evidence tissue_free row 3, dg_marker option 1.

options.label: Imaging shows a tumour of the colon or rectum, the report calls serum carcinoembryonic antigen raised, and the file calls it colorectal cancer
options.reason: A raised carcinoembryonic antigen with a colorectal cancer shown on imaging registers the cancer without its type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, Table 4). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 4. ICCC-3 places that code at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7. Visser O, et al. Front Oncol 2023;13:1250549, Table 4, p. 06, read from the page image (contract §0.5), with rule 6, p. 05 (basis 4 never stands alone). Colorectal cancer, carcinoembryonic antigen: 8000/3, XIIb at the routed sites, so the referral names refer_code 8000.

options.label: Imaging shows a malignant tumour, at least probable, and no marker result above registers it
options.reason: Imaging alone does not establish the tumour's type, and a marker registers a code only with the diagnosis it names (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5 and Table 4). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 2. ICCC-3 places that code at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: A marker is raised, but the imaging shows no tumour
options.reason: A raised tumour marker is not registered unless a clinical investigation shows the tumour (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 6).

options.label: Imaging calls it possible only, or describes a benign lesion
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.question: The cytology report is not diagnostic, and no histology report is in the file. What does the imaging report conclude?
nodes.hint: Answer from the radiologist's own conclusion. Imaging alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser 2023 rule 5, p. 03: imaging alone is 8000/3 at basis 2, a Group XII code at this tree's sites. Evidence context 'cytology': reached with evidence_tests ['Cytology', 'Imaging'], which no option changes.

options.label: Imaging shows a malignant tumour, at least probable
options.reason: Imaging alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 2. ICCC-3 places that code at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Imaging calls it possible only, or describes a benign lesion
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.question: What does the cytology report conclude?
nodes.hint: Use the cytology report's own conclusion. Cytology gives basis of diagnosis 5; a histology report gives the full type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D8: cytology naming an entity codes it at basis 5 (Visser 2023 Table 1, p. 03); malignant cells with no type refer to Group XII with 8001; suspicious is not registrable (rule 4).

options.label: Mucinous adenocarcinoma, or colloid carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Mucinous adenocarcinoma (8480/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence dg_cytology option 1 (a named type) with the paediatric type of dg_colorectal_histology (departure 4).

options.label: Signet ring cell carcinoma

options.label: Neuroendocrine tumour, or carcinoid

options.label: Cytology names a carcinoma without naming its type

options.label: Lymphoma
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the colon, rectum or anus keeps the colon, rectum or anus as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. The hop carries the case's site.

options.label: Malignant cells are present, with no tumour type named
options.reason: Cytology establishes malignant cells but no tumour type. It is registered as Tumor cells, malignant (8001/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. ICCC-3 places that code at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report and a chromogranin A, serotonin or carcinoembryonic antigen result are in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves the marker route (Visser Table 4) as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report, with no chromogranin A, serotonin or carcinoembryonic antigen result, is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves imaging as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and no imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology and no imaging leave the note as the best evidence; Cytology stays on the case (Group 10's split).

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. When the report gives two tumour types for one tumour and no answer covers both, choose the answer with the higher code (WHO coding Rule K). A mucinous adenocarcinoma with a tubular component is 8480.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence dg_colorectal_histology (departures 5 and 6). D1: the paediatric entities are mucinous adenocarcinoma, signet ring cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, adenocarcinoma in familial adenomatous polyposis and tubular adenocarcinoma (Polat 2021, Mahajan 2022); the neuroendocrine tumour is an option because its code needs the grade. The Rule K example is Polat 2021 Table 1 (MA + TA), which the evidence records 8480/3.

options.label: Mucinous adenocarcinoma, or colloid carcinoma

options.coding_note: D1: Polat 2021, Mahajan 2022.

options.coding_note: D1: Mahajan 2022.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe tumour cells holding mucin inside the cell, with signet ring cells making up more than half of the tumour.

options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3). The grade is not part of the code.

ICCC-3 places that code at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.

options.label: Lymphoma, for example Burkitt lymphoma

options.label: Leukaemia, or leukaemic infiltration
options.reason: Leukaemic infiltration of the colon, rectum or anus is coded as the leukaemia, in ICCC-3 Group I, and a leukaemia is recorded at the bone marrow (C42.1). Code the case from the Group I (leukaemias) tree.
options.coding_note: WHO Rule E (section 4.2.8): every leukaemia except myeloid sarcoma is C42.1, so the hop carries the marrow. A myeloid sarcoma option is not built: check_leukaemia_referrals_record_marrow admits a site-keeping Group I referral only on the nodes it lists.

options.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST)
options.reason: A gastrointestinal stromal tumour is registered as Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (8936/3), which ICCC-3 places at the colon, rectum or anus in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence dg_colorectal_histology option 9 (refer to Group 12, 8936/3). ICCC-2017 XIIa1 at C18.0-C21.8; refer_code names the code Group XII records.

options.label: A sarcoma, for example rhabdomyosarcoma or clear cell sarcoma
options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the colon, rectum or anus belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 places 8800-8921 and 9120-9133 in Group IX at the Group XI sites; a bone sarcoma arises in bone, which no Group XI tree routes.

options.label: Teratoma or another germ cell tumour
options.reason: Germ cell tumours, teratomas among them, belong to ICCC-3 Group X at the colon, rectum or anus. Code the case from the Group X (germ cell tumours) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 range 101 (Xb2) places 9080-9084 at the extragonadal sites.

options.label: Another malignant tumour the report names that is not a carcinoma or melanoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 Group XII holds the specified malignant tumours no other group codes. Code the case from the Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) tree.

nodes.question: Which grade does the report give the neuroendocrine tumour?
nodes.hint: If the report gives two grades, or the Ki-67 index and the mitotic count point to different grades, choose the higher grade (WHO coding Rule G). A neuroendocrine carcinoma (poorly differentiated, small cell or large cell) is the last answer. When the report names the tumour's cell type or hormone as well as a grade, choose the answer with the higher code (WHO coding Rule K): grade 2 and grade 3 (8249) are higher than every cell-type or hormone code; with grade 1 or no grade, take the last answer and find the named type.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence dg_net_grade (departure 8). ICD-O-3.2: 8240/3 Neuroendocrine tumor, NOS holds grade 1 as a related term; 8249/3 Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2 holds grade 3 as a related term. D1 exception: the code depends on the grade.

options.label: Grade 1 (G1)
options.reason: Recorded as Neuroendocrine tumor, NOS (8240/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 1 as a related term of this code.
options.recognition_aid: Ki-67 index below 3% and fewer than 2 mitoses per 2 mm2.

options.label: Grade 2 (G2), or atypical carcinoid
options.reason: Recorded as Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2 (8249/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Atypical carcinoid tumor as a synonym of this code.
options.recognition_aid: Ki-67 index from 3% to 20%, or 2 to 20 mitoses per 2 mm2.

options.label: Grade 3 (G3), and the report still calls the tumour well differentiated
options.reason: Recorded as Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2 (8249/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 3 as a related term of this code.
options.coding_note: Evidence data gap 4 (the option rests on Pfister 2022's listing of appendiceal neuroendocrine tumours).
options.recognition_aid: Ki-67 index above 20%, or more than 20 mitoses per 2 mm2, in a tumour the report calls well differentiated.

options.label: No grade stated, or carcinoid with no grade
options.reason: Recorded as Neuroendocrine tumor, NOS (8240/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Carcinoid tumor, NOS as a synonym of this code.
options.upgrade_path: The report does not state the grade. A report that gives grade 2 or grade 3 records Neuroendocrine tumor, grade 2 (8249/3): go back and take the option that names it.

options.label: Neuroendocrine carcinoma (poorly differentiated, small cell or large cell), a mixed tumour with a neuroendocrine component, or a tumour the report names by its cell type or hormone, such as an enterochromaffin cell (serotonin-producing) tumour - type its name to find it
options.coding_note: Evidence dg_net_grade option 5 (to dg_carcinoma_picker), with the Rule K cell-type case (departure 8).

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the colon, rectum or anus are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer. A report that states invasion, or diagnoses an invasive carcinoma arising in the lesion, is answered from the carcinoma options: go back to the step before.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. Evidence dg_not_malignant_gut, split by tree (departure 9).

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the appendix?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A tumour reported only in the tissue beside the appendix and caecum, such as retrocaecal tissue, is not a tumour of the appendix: ICD-O-3.1 lists that tissue under the retroperitoneum (C48.0), so go back to the site step. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.

nodes.question: Which grade does the report give the neuroendocrine tumour?
nodes.hint: If the report gives two grades, or the Ki-67 index and the mitotic count point to different grades, choose the higher grade (WHO coding Rule G). When the report names the tumour's cell type or hormone as well as a grade, choose the answer with the higher code (WHO coding Rule K): grade 2 and grade 3 (8249) are higher than every cell-type or hormone code; with grade 1 or no grade, take the last answer and find the named type.

nodes.question: What is in the file for this lung tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. Cytology of sputum, a bronchial washing or brushing, or a needle aspirate counts as cytology. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected cancer does not register it.

Evidence lu_evidence, lu_lab and lu_cytology (departures 2 to 4 in the module docstring).

nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D8: cytology naming an entity codes it at basis 5 (Visser 2023 Table 1, p. 03); malignant cells with no type refer to Group XII with 8001; suspicious is not registrable (rule 4).

options.label: Carcinoid tumour or neuroendocrine tumour
options.reason: Recorded as Neuroendocrine tumor, NOS (8240/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. ICD-O-3.2 gives Carcinoid tumor, NOS as a synonym of this code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence lu_cytology option 1 (departure 4).

options.label: Small cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Small cell carcinoma, NOS (8041/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence lu_cytology option 1 (departure 4).

options.label: Non-small cell carcinoma, with no type named, including one the report says favours a type
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_cytology option 1 and lu_picker option 25 (departures 4, 7). Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6): the favoured type is coded when the file confirms it (SEER lung rule H3), and the stains decide the favoured type (Nicholson 2022, PDF pp. 5-6).

options.label: Adenocarcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Departure 4: a paediatric type of the histology screen a cytology report can name.

options.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS (8070/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Departure 4: a paediatric type of the histology screen a cytology report can name.

options.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8430/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8. Departure 4: a paediatric type of the histology screen a cytology report can name.

options.label: A carcinoma whose type the cytology report does not name, or names a type not listed above
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. A type this list does not hold is recorded with the generic carcinoma code; a histology report gives the type's own code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence lu_cytology option 2, widened to the named types the list does not hold (departure 4; standing rule 8).

options.label: Lymphoma
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the lung keeps the lung as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. The hop carries the case's site.

options.label: Malignant cells are present, with no tumour type named
options.reason: Cytology establishes malignant cells but no tumour type. It is registered as Tumor cells, malignant (8001/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. ICCC-3 places that code at the lung in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report and a chromogranin A, serotonin or adrenocorticotropic hormone result are in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves the marker route (Visser Table 4) as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report, with no chromogranin A, serotonin or adrenocorticotropic hormone result, is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves imaging as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and no imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology and no imaging leave the note as the best evidence; Cytology stays on the case (Group 10's split).

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Choose the name in the report's diagnosis line. A tumour that the report says has spread to the lung from another organ is a deposit: it is coded at the organ where it began. Adenosquamous carcinoma and combined small cell carcinoma each have their own code: find them under another carcinoma the report names.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology (departures 5 to 13). D1: the paediatric entities are carcinoid tumour, mucoepidermoid carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, squamous cell carcinoma, small cell carcinoma, large cell carcinoma and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (Ozkan 2024, Chen 2026; evidence §11). D12: NUT carcinoma (Nicholson 2022, p. 3; Pfister 2022, p. 14).

options.label: Carcinoid tumour, typical or atypical carcinoid, or neuroendocrine tumour
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024, Chen 2026 (evidence §11).

options.label: Mucoepidermoid carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8430/3).
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024, Chen 2026.
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe a mix of mucus-secreting, squamous and intermediate cells.

options.label: Adenocarcinoma, with no subtype named
options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3).
options.upgrade_path: The report does not name a subtype. A report that names one (for example lepidic, papillary, micropapillary, solid or invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma) gives that subtype's own code: go back and take another carcinoma the report names.
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024.

options.label: Acinar adenocarcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3). ICD-O-3.2 places acinar adenocarcinoma of the lung on a code whose Preferred term it marks obsolete, and no screen offers that code until the registrar rules, so the generic adenocarcinoma code is recorded. This awaits the registrar's decision.
options.coding_note: D3: 8551/3 Preferred term [obs], Related term Acinar adenocarcinoma of lung live (currency check §4); departure 8.
options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the type the report names; it does not change this code.

options.label: Squamous cell carcinoma, with no subtype named
options.reason: Recorded as Squamous cell carcinoma, NOS (8070/3).
options.upgrade_path: The report does not name a subtype. A report that names one (keratinizing, non-keratinizing or basaloid squamous cell carcinoma) gives that subtype's own code: go back and take another carcinoma the report names.
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024.

options.label: Small cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Small cell carcinoma, NOS (8041/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Small cell neuroendocrine carcinoma as a related term of this code.
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024, Chen 2026.

options.label: Large cell carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Large cell carcinoma, NOS (8012/3).
options.coding_note: D1: Ozkan 2024.

options.label: Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma, including combined large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma
options.reason: Recorded as Large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (8013/3). ICD-O-3.2 gives Combined large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma as a related term of this code.
options.coding_note: D1: Chen 2026.
options.recognition_aid: A tumour that looks like a carcinoid but has a mitotic count above the atypical carcinoid range is called large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma.

options.label: Non-small cell carcinoma, with no type named, including one the report says favours a type
options.coding_note: Moved from the evidence's picker (departure 7). Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6): the favoured type is coded when the file confirms it (SEER lung rule H3), and the stains decide the favoured type (Nicholson 2022, PDF pp. 5-6).

options.label: Pleuropulmonary blastoma
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes it as Pleuropulmonary blastoma (8973/3). ICCC-3 places that code in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 8; ICCC-2017 XIIa3 at every site (evidence conflicts, Group 12).

options.label: Pulmonary blastoma
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes it as Pulmonary blastoma (8972/3). ICCC-3 places that code in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 9; ICCC-2017 XIIa3.
options.recognition_aid: Pulmonary blastoma and pleuropulmonary blastoma are different tumours; choose the one the report names.

options.label: Paraganglioma
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes it as Paraganglioma, NOS (8680/3), or Extra-adrenal paraganglioma, NOS (8693/3) when the report says it arises outside the adrenal gland. ICCC-3 places both codes in Group IV (neuroblastoma and other peripheral nervous cell tumours), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group IV tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 10; ICCC-2017 IVb at every site.
options.recognition_aid: Paraganglioma and carcinoid tumour can look alike; choose the one the report names.

options.label: Carcinoma, with no type named
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3).
options.upgrade_path: The report does not state the tumour's type. A report that names it gives that type's own code: go back and take the option that names it.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 21; the generic option of the screen (D4's nearest generic code). A non-small cell carcinoma takes the option above, whose stain panel is lu_nscc_ihc.

options.label: Melanoma
options.coding_note: D13: cross-tree next_node into the melanoma tree (me_mucosa), which offers every XId code. group11_tree.trees() defers this hop while g11_melanoma has no module.

options.label: NUT carcinoma (also written NUT midline carcinoma, BRD4::NUTM1 carcinoma or carcinoma with t(15;19) translocation), or a carcinoma reported with a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene result
options.coding_note: D12: NUT carcinoma evidence (NUT_carcinoma.json, nut_site_option).
options.recognition_aid: Reports describe a poorly differentiated or undifferentiated carcinoma, sometimes with abrupt keratinization, and nuclear staining for NUT.

options.label: Another carcinoma the report names - type its name to find it
options.coding_note: D2: the Group XI picker.

options.label: A benign tumour, a precursor lesion or an in situ carcinoma, such as adenocarcinoma in situ, a papilloma, a hamartoma, sclerosing pneumocytoma, a congenital peribronchial myofibroblastic tumour or a fetal lung interstitial tumour
options.coding_note: The exclusion screen (contract §4.2).

options.label: A deposit of a tumour that began elsewhere
Malignant tumour, type not determined by the report
options.reason: The report establishes a malignant tumour without determining its type. It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3). ICCC-3 places that code at the lung in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Lymphoma, including Hodgkin lymphoma, or Langerhans cell histiocytosis or Erdheim-Chester disease
options.reason: Lymphomas and histiocytic tumours belong to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the lung keeps the lung as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas and reticuloendothelial neoplasms) tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 14 (departure 11). ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. ICCC-2017 holds no range for 9749 Erdheim-Chester disease; the Group II tree carries it (evidence conflicts, Group 2).

options.label: Leukaemia, or leukaemic infiltration
options.reason: Leukaemic infiltration of the lung is coded as the leukaemia, in ICCC-3 Group I, and a leukaemia is recorded at the bone marrow (C42.1). Code the case from the Group I (leukaemias) tree.
options.coding_note: WHO Rule E (section 4.2.8): every leukaemia except myeloid sarcoma is C42.1, so the hop carries the marrow. A myeloid sarcoma option is not built: check_leukaemia_referrals_record_marrow admits a site-keeping Group I referral only on the nodes it lists.

options.label: A sarcoma, such as rhabdomyosarcoma, Ewing sarcoma, alveolar soft part sarcoma, intimal sarcoma, pulmonary myxoid sarcoma or malignant perivascular epithelioid tumour (PEComa)
options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the lung belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue and other extraosseous sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 15 with the paediatric sarcomas of Chen 2026 (departure 11, evidence data gap 10).

options.label: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes an inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour as Myofibroblastic tumor, NOS (8825/1), behaviour 1, uncertain, and a myofibroblastic sarcoma as Myofibroblastic sarcoma (8825/3), which ICCC-3 places in Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue and other extraosseous sarcomas) tree, which records whether the report's tumour is registered.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 17 was an exclusion (8825/1); referred to Group IX on the controller's instruction (departure 11). The Group IX screen g9_soft_tissue st_fibroblastic holds the exclusion and 8825/3.

options.label: Teratoma or another germ cell tumour
options.reason: Germ cell tumours, teratomas among them, belong to ICCC-3 Group X at the lung. Code the case from the Group X (germ cell tumours) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 range 101 (Xb2) places 9080-9084 at the extragonadal sites.

options.label: Another malignant tumour the report names that is not a carcinoma or melanoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 Group XII holds the specified malignant tumours no other group codes. Code the case from the Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) tree.

options.label: Carcinosarcoma
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes it as Carcinosarcoma, NOS (8980/3). ICCC-3 places that code in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 11; ICCC-2017 XIIa4 (evidence conflicts, Group 12).

options.label: Myoepithelial carcinoma
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes it as Myoepithelial carcinoma (8982/3). ICCC-3 places that code in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence lu_histology option 12; ICCC-2017 XIIa4.

nodes.question: The histology report calls the tumour a non-small cell carcinoma and states no definite type. Does a doctor elsewhere in the file state the type, or is the patient treated for one type?
nodes.hint: A report that says the carcinoma "favours" adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, or gives stains that point to one, has not stated the type. The type is recorded only when the file confirms it: a doctor (an oncologist, a chest physician, a surgeon or a later pathology report) states it, or the patient is treated for it. This is the lung rule for uncertain terms of the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program's Solid Tumor Rules.
nodes.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Asked before the favoured type because an ihc_checklist rule is a terminal.

options.label: Yes: a doctor states adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, or the patient is treated for one of them
options.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Condition 1 (physician confirmation) or 2 (treatment).

options.label: No, or the file says nothing more about the type
options.reason: Recorded as Non-small cell carcinoma (8046/3). A report that says the carcinoma favours a type, or gives stains that point to one, has not stated the type, and nothing else in the file confirms it.
options.upgrade_path: The file does not confirm a type. A later pathology report or a doctor's note that states adenocarcinoma or squamous cell carcinoma, or treatment for one, gives that type's code: go back and answer yes.
options.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Neither condition holds: non-small cell carcinoma, NOS (Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 6, Table 3).

nodes.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 5 (TTF-1, mucin, p40) and PDF p. 6, Table 3.

options.upgrade_path: Immunohistochemistry, where the report does not describe it, confirms the type the report names; it does not change this code.

nodes.question: Answer each stain as the histology report states it.
nodes.hint: Answer positive or negative, and 'Not done or not readable' for a stain the report does not mention. TTF-1 or a mucin stain points to adenocarcinoma; p40 points to squamous cell carcinoma.
nodes.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 5 (TTF-1, mucin, p40) and PDF p. 6, Table 3. Both TTF-1 and p40 positive, or neither stain and no mucin, fall to non-small cell carcinoma, NOS (Table 3).

resolution_logic.reason: TTF-1 is positive and p40 is not: the WHO calls this non-small cell carcinoma, favour adenocarcinoma. The pathology report favours this type, and the file confirms it: a doctor states it, or the patient is treated for it. Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3).

resolution_logic.reason: A mucin stain is positive and p40 is not: the WHO calls this non-small cell carcinoma, favour adenocarcinoma. The pathology report favours this type, and the file confirms it: a doctor states it, or the patient is treated for it. Recorded as Adenocarcinoma, NOS (8140/3).
resolution_logic.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 5: 'the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma can be supported if mucin stains are positive'.

resolution_logic.coding_note: Registrar, 8 October 2026 (review A2, E6). SEER Solid Tumor Rules, lung, rule H3 (added 12 October 2018). Nicholson 2022, PDF p. 6, Table 3: 'supported by stains (i.e., p40+)'.

nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A fine-needle aspiration report counts as cytology. A pathology report on a biopsy or a resection counts as histology. A report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A germ cell tumour diagnosed from imaging with a raised alpha-fetoprotein or human chorionic gonadotropin is coded from the Group X tree, which has its own route for it: go back and choose Group X (germ cell, trophoblastic and gonadal tumours).

nodes.question: Which thymic tumour does the histology report name?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. When the report lists more than one thymoma type in one tumour, choose the type with the higher code number (WHO coding Rule K): A 8581, AB 8582, B1 8583, B2 8584, B3 8585. Type AB is a single type. A thymoma combined with a thymic carcinoma or carcinoid in one tumour is coded the same way: every thymoma code is higher than every thymic carcinoma and carcinoid code except Thymic carcinoma, NOS (8586). A name written thymic carcinoma, hepatoid type is the same tumour as a hepatoid carcinoma of the thymus: the word thymic names the site. Record the type's code, not Thymic carcinoma, NOS (8586/3). Thymic carcinoma, NOS is a not-otherwise-specified term, so a specified type replaces it; this is not a choice by the higher code (WHO coding Rule K), because a not-otherwise-specified term and a specified type are not two modifiers that no single code covers.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence tm_histology options 1-6 (departure 5), tm_picker options 9 and 16 (departures 9 and 10). nodes.question: What does the file report for this tumour?
nodes.hint: Choose the first answer that matches the file. Keratin, p63, p40 and CD99 stains do not decide NUT carcinoma; a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene test does.

options.coding_note: Luo 2025, p. 2 and p. 5 ('most often in the abdomen, soft tissue or central nervous system').

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the thymus or mediastinum are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. The four exclusions and the hyperplasia line of evidence tm_histology (departures 5 and 12).

nodes.question: What is in the file about this melanoma?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or excision counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. An immunohistochemistry or gene report is read with the histology report it belongs to; on its own it does not register a melanoma.

nodes.question: Where did the melanoma arise?
nodes.hint: A melanoma of the arm, leg, trunk, chin or forehead with no tissue named is a melanoma of the skin of that region. A site named with a prefix such as peri- or para- takes the tissue the report names. A melanoma that spans two skin regions with no stated point of origin takes the overlapping-lesion code (.8). ICD-O prints skin (C44) beside many melanoma names: when the report names another site, record that site once the report shows the tumour there is not a deposit.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: If the report names two melanoma types for one tumour, record the type with the higher code number (WHO coding Rule K): an amelanotic Spitz melanoma is recorded as Malignant Spitz tumor (8770/3), and an acral nodular melanoma as Acral melanoma (8744/3). A tumour the report calls intermediate, of uncertain malignant potential, in situ or a naevus is on the screen for tumours that are not malignant. Take the Spitz option when the diagnosis line says spitzoid melanoma, Spitz melanoma or malignant Spitz tumour. A melanoma described as spitzoid only in the microscopic description, with a diagnosis of melanoma, is Malignant melanoma, NOS (8720/3).

nodes.question: What is in the file for this skin tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a curettage, shave, punch or excision biopsy counts as histology. An immunohistochemistry or gene report on its own does not stand in for a histology report. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A carcinoma the report places at a body region with no tissue named, such as the arm, the leg, the back, the chin or the forehead, is recorded at the skin of that region (WHO coding Rule A). A tumour across two skin regions whose starting point the report does not give is recorded at overlapping lesion of skin, C44.8 (WHO coding Rule C): go back to the site step to change the site. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's own term. If the report states that the tumour is benign, in situ or of uncertain malignant potential, choose that answer, even for a tumour type that is usually malignant. A named subtype of basal cell or squamous cell carcinoma (nodular, superficial, infiltrating, keratinizing and others), Merkel cell carcinoma, and the adnexal carcinomas (sweat gland, hair follicle or sebaceous) are found under another carcinoma the report names. When one tumour shows two types and no single answer names both, choose the higher code (WHO coding Rule K): a Merkel cell carcinoma combined with squamous cell carcinoma is recorded as Merkel cell carcinoma (8247/3). Paget disease of the nipple or breast is coded at the breast: go back to the site step.

nodes.question: Where on the body does the report place the tumour?
nodes.hint: A carcinoma the report places at a body region with no tissue named (the arm, the leg, the back, the chin, the forehead) is recorded at the skin of that region (WHO coding Rule A). A site written with peri- or para- is the skin of that region when the tumour is a skin carcinoma (Rule B). Basal cell carcinoma and the other skin carcinomas of the vulva, penis or scrotum are recorded at the vulva, the penis or the scrotum, which ICD-O names as other primary sites of basal cell carcinoma (Rule H). For the eyelid, the external ear, the skin of the lip, or a named part of the vulva or penis, go back to the site step. The next screen asks the tumour type again.
nodes.coding_note: Departure 4: the options of evidence sk_site that correct the site the router recorded (D9; Rule A, Rules p. 1 and p. 4; Rule H, Table 23, Rules p. 10). Each captures the topography and returns to the histology screen, the salivary tree's sg_site pattern. Every code the histology screen emits is a Group XI code at C44.3, C44.5-C44.7, C51.9, C60.9 and C63.2 (routed sites of this tree). options.label: The diagnosis names NUT carcinoma or NUT midline carcinoma

options.label: The diagnosis names another carcinoma (for example poorly differentiated carcinoma), and the file reports a NUT immunostain or a NUTM1 gene test
