decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the breast (C50.0-C50.9; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this breast tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A core needle biopsy, excision or mastectomy report counts as histology; an immunohistochemistry or gene report on its own does not stand in for one. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. The site step records the part of the breast the report names. A report that gives only a clock-face position is recorded at breast, part not stated (C50.9). One tumour that crosses two or more parts, with no stated origin, is recorded at overlapping lesion of breast (C50.8). A periareolar or retroareolar carcinoma is a breast tumour. A tumour of the skin of the breast is a skin tumour, recorded at the skin of the trunk (C44.5): go back to the site step and record C44.5. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence br_document_inventory, br_clinical, br_imaging and br_cytology (departures 1 to 4 in the module docstring).

options.label: A referral letter or clinical note only - no imaging report, no tissue
An imaging report only (mammogram, ultrasound or magnetic resonance imaging) - no tissue
A cytology report (a fine-needle aspirate or a smear) - no histology report
A histology report (core needle biopsy, excision or mastectomy), with or without immunohistochemistry or gene reports

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type. A melanoma of the skin of the breast is a skin tumour: go back to the site step and record the skin of the trunk (C44.5).
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the breast in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.hint: Use the cytology report's own conclusion. Cytology gives basis of diagnosis 5; a histology report gives the full type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D8: cytology naming an entity codes it at basis 5 (Visser 2023 Table 1, p. 03); malignant cells with no type refer to Group XII with 8001; suspicious is not registrable (rule 4).

options.label: Cytology names a carcinoma, with or without naming its type
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. The type of a breast carcinoma is not settled on a limited sample, so a type the cytology report names does not change the code.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence br_cytology option 1 and tissue_free row 4.
options.upgrade_path: A histology report gives the carcinoma's type and that type's own code.

options.label: Cytology names a melanoma
options.reason: Recorded as Malignant melanoma, NOS (8720/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it. A melanoma that began elsewhere, such as the skin, is coded at that primary site: go back to the site step and record it.
options.coding_note: D8. Evidence br_cytology option 2 (departure 4): D8 in place of the hop to the melanoma tree, whose screens record basis 7.

options.label: Cytology names a lymphoma
options.reason: A lymphoma belongs to ICCC-3 Group II. A lymphoma that arises in the breast keeps the breast as its site (WHO Rule D: an extranodal lymphoma is coded to its site of origin). Code the case from the Group II (lymphomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICD-O-3.1 Rule D, p. 15. The hop carries the case's site.

options.label: Cytology names a sarcoma
options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the breast belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 places 8800-8921 and 9120-9133 in Group IX at the Group XI sites; a bone sarcoma arises in bone, which no Group XI tree routes.

options.reason: Not registrable. Whether a phyllodes tumour is malignant is decided on histology, so the case is not registered from this report.
options.coding_note: Evidence br_cytology option 5.

options.label: Malignant cells are present, with no tumour type named
options.reason: Cytology establishes malignant cells but no tumour type. It is registered as Tumor cells, malignant (8001/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. ICCC-3 places that code at the breast in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's own term. When a core needle biopsy and a later excision both name a type, use the excision report. If the report states that the tumour is benign, in situ or of uncertain malignant potential, choose that answer, even for a tumour type that is usually malignant. An in situ carcinoma with microinvasion (invasion of 1 mm or less) is an invasive carcinoma: choose the invasive type the report names. A tumour of the skin of the breast is a skin tumour, recorded at the skin of the trunk (C44.5): go back to the site step and record C44.5.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence br_histology (departures 5 to 7). D1: the paediatric entities are secretory carcinoma (common) and invasive ductal, invasive lobular, medullary, inflammatory and anaplastic carcinoma (Sosnowska-Sienkiewicz 2024, section 72; registrar, 8 October 2026), and malignant phyllodes tumour (sections 2 and 76) on the fibroepithelial screen; the papillary carcinomas are options because their codes need the invasion answer.

nodes.question: Which carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: Type part of the name in the box and the matching options appear. The other names ICD-O-3.2 gives a tumour find it too. Use the report's own term. A carcinoma first diagnosed outside the breast is coded at its primary site. If a compound name is not found, search for its parts in the other order (WHO coding Rule J). A carcinoma of no special type mixed with lobular carcinoma is Infiltrating duct and lobular carcinoma (8522/3); mixed with another special type it is Infiltrating duct mixed with other types of carcinoma (8523/3). When one tumour carries two type names and no single option names both, choose the higher code number (WHO coding Rule K): a metaplastic squamous cell carcinoma is recorded as Metaplastic carcinoma, NOS (8575/3). A name that places the tumour in another organ, such as the lung, pancreas, thymus or ovary, means a deposit unless the report says the tumour began in the breast: go back and choose the deposit answer.

decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the female genital organs (C51.0-C51.8, C52.9-C55.9, C57.0-C58.9; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the vulva, vagina, cervix, uterus or another female genital organ?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology, and a cervical or vaginal smear counts as cytology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. The site is the part the report says the tumour began in: a tumour that involves two parts whose origin the report does not state is an overlapping lesion of the female genital organs (C57.8). A carcinoma of the skin of the perineum or groin is a skin tumour, not a vulval one. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence fg_evidence and fg_cytology (departures 2 and 3 in the module docstring). No laboratory screen and no marker tier: the evidence names no laboratory test, and no Visser Table 4 row concerns these sites.

options.label: A referral letter or clinical note only - no imaging report, no tissue
An imaging report only (ultrasound, computed tomography or magnetic resonance imaging) - no tissue
A cytology report (a cervical or vaginal smear, or a fine-needle aspirate) - no histology report
A histology report, with or without immunohistochemistry or gene reports

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the female genital organs in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: The cytology report is not diagnostic, and no imaging report or histology report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'cytology': reached with evidence_tests ['Cytology'], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the female genital organs in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

nodes.question: No tissue is in the file. What does the imaging report conclude?

nodes.hint: Use the cytology report's own conclusion. Cytology gives basis of diagnosis 5; a histology report gives the full type. A squamous or glandular intraepithelial lesion on a smear is not an invasive cancer.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D8: cytology naming an entity codes it at basis 5 (Visser 2023 Table 1, p. 03); malignant cells with no type refer to Group XII with 8001; suspicious is not registrable (rule 4).

options.coding_note: Evidence fg_cytology option 4 (departure 3: its 'suspicious for carcinoma' part is the common suspicious line).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves imaging as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and no imaging report is in the file

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. If the report says the tumour began in another organ, it is a deposit: choose the deposit line. An option that names an organ in brackets belongs to that organ: take it only when the site recorded is that organ. Gastric-type, endometrioid, serous, mucinous, intestinal-type and the other named carcinomas are under another carcinoma the report names; an adenocarcinoma called HPV-associated or HPV-independent that also names one of those types takes that type (WHO coding Rule K). An adenocarcinoma the report calls mesonephric-like is not a mesonephric adenocarcinoma: ICD-O-3.2 has no code for it, so take adenocarcinoma with no type named.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence fg_histology, with fg_picker's referral lines (departures 4 to 8). D1: clear cell adenocarcinoma at the cervix and vagina, adenocarcinoma at the cervix and uterus and squamous cell carcinoma at the vulva (Wohlmuth 2021, SEER-18, ages 0 to 18). D4: 8483, 8484 and 9113 are not built; registrar questions 1 and 2. D5: departure 5.

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the female genital organs are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer. If the same report also names an invasive carcinoma, go back and choose the carcinoma.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. Evidence fg_not_invasive, with fg_histology's benign line (departure 11).

nodes.question: Where does the report say the primary tumour is?
nodes.hint: The tumour in the female genital organs is a deposit, not a separate registration: the case is coded at its primary site. A melanoma is answered at the step before, from the melanoma option. A carcinoma of the vagina in a patient who has or had a carcinoma of the cervix is taken as the cervical carcinoma's spread unless the report states otherwise.

nodes.question: Which carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: Type part of the name in the box and the matching options appear. The other names ICD-O-3.2 gives a tumour find it too. Use the report's own term. A carcinoma first diagnosed outside the female genital organs is coded at its primary site. When the report gives a neuroendocrine tumour two grades, choose the higher grade (WHO coding Rule G). A carcinoma type that usually begins in another organ, such as intestinal-type adenocarcinoma, adenocarcinoma of mammary-like glands or Merkel cell carcinoma, is recorded here only when the report says it began here (WHO coding Rule H). Mucinous carcinoma, gastric type (8482/3) prints the cervix beside it. When the report places it in the uterine corpus, record 8482/3 at the corpus, not Adenocarcinoma, intestinal type (8144/3).

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the urinary tract or male genital organs?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy, transurethral resection or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A urachal carcinoma, at the bladder dome or anterior wall and centred in the bladder wall, is recorded at the urachus (C67.7). A renal pelvis tumour that invades the kidney stays at the renal pelvis (C65.9). One tumour across two parts of the bladder whose origin the report does not give is recorded at overlapping lesion of bladder (C67.8); across two urinary organs at C68.8; across two male genital organs at C63.8; across two parts of the penis at C60.8. A report that names only the tissue around an organ, such as perivesical, periprostatic or periurethral tissue, does not name that organ. If the site recorded does not follow these rules, go back to the site step. A raised prostate-specific antigen alone does not register a tumour, and a report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.

Urine cytology cannot tell an invasive carcinoma from urothelial carcinoma in situ, which Group XI does not register; a histology report decides. This awaits the registrar's decision.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. An option that names organs in brackets belongs to those organs: take it only when the site recorded is one of them. A tumour with any urothelial component, including urothelial carcinoma in situ, is a urothelial carcinoma, except a neuroendocrine carcinoma: find that under another carcinoma the report names. When the report gives two terms for one tumour and no single option covers both, choose the one with the higher code (WHO coding Rule K). Ductal adenocarcinoma and basal cell carcinoma of the prostate are found under another carcinoma the report names and keep the prostate as the site (WHO coding Rule H).
nodes.coding_note: Evidence gu_urinary_histology, gu_prostate_histology, gu_penis_histology and gu_male_genital_histology, merged (D14; departures 5 to 13). D1: invasive urothelial carcinoma is the one carcinoma a paediatric source reports at these organs (Liu 2025, bladder only; data gaps 7 and 8); penile squamous cell carcinoma is an option because its code needs the subtype and HPV status. Rule G: no screen offers a grade (evidence rules_a_to_k G).

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?

A non-invasive papillary urothelial carcinoma is pTa and urothelial carcinoma in situ is pTis. If the report states invasion of the lamina propria (subepithelial connective tissue) or deeper (pT1 or higher), or an invasive carcinoma beside the lesion, go back and choose the invasive carcinoma.

decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the eye (C69.0-C69.9; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the eye, the lacrimal gland or the orbit?
nodes.hint: A radiology or ultrasound report counts as imaging. A cytology report on a fine-needle aspirate or fluid counts as cytology. A pathology report on a biopsy or excision counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A file that names retinoblastoma or retinocytoma is recorded in Group V, which registers it on an eye examination or imaging, because a biopsy of the eye is usually avoided: do not code it from this tree, and code it from the Group V tree. Choose the tier that matches the reports for any other tumour. A tumour of the eyelid is a skin tumour (C44.1): go back to the site step. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence ey_evidence and ey_cytology (departures 1 and 9 in the module docstring).

nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the eye, the lacrimal gland or the orbit in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

ICCC-3 places that code at the eye, the lacrimal gland or the orbit in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's own term. A carcinoma of the eye is recorded at the part of the eye the report names. If the site step recorded the eye with no part named (C69.9) or with more than one part (C69.8), and the report names the part where the tumour began (the conjunctiva, cornea, retina, choroid, ciliary body, lacrimal gland or orbit), choose the answer that records the part. Squamous intraepithelial neoplasia, dysplasia and carcinoma in situ of the conjunctiva or cornea, and the benign tumours of the lacrimal gland, have not invaded and are found under the answer for a benign, borderline or in situ tumour. A tumour the report places at the limbus, where the cornea meets the conjunctiva, is recorded at the cornea (C69.1). Squamous cell carcinoma and adenocarcinoma of the conjunctiva, the lacrimal gland, the ciliary body or the retinal pigment epithelium are found under another carcinoma the report names. A tumour of the eyelid is a skin tumour.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence ey_surface_histology, ey_lacrimal_histology, ey_intraocular_histology and ey_orbit_histology, as one screen (departure 3, D14). Carcinomas of every type are picker entries (departure 7); Milman 2023 and Pfister 2022 Table 3 report no eye carcinoma in children. The unstated-type option is the generic option. Melanoma hops to me_eye (D13); T2c to confirm the screen takes a melanoma of the conjunctiva, the intraocular structures, the lacrimal drainage system and the orbit.

nodes.question: Which part of the eye does the report name as the place where the tumour began?
nodes.hint: Use this question only when the site step recorded the eye with the part not stated (C69.9) or with more than one part (C69.8), and the histology report or the operation note names the part where the tumour began (WHO coding Rule H). A tumour the report places at the limbus, where the cornea meets the conjunctiva, is recorded at the cornea (C69.1). A tumour of the eyelid is a skin tumour: go back to the site step. A site named only by a prefix such as peri- is not an ICD-O site: go back to the site step. The next screen asks the tumour type again.
nodes.coding_note: Departure 2: the part-of-eye options of evidence ey_site (D9; Rule H). Each captures the topography and returns to ey_histology, the salivary tree's sg_site pattern. The evidence's C69.8 and C69.9 options, the eyelid, the optic nerve, the periorbital region and the deposit are the router's, other screens' or other trees'. Every code ey_histology emits is a Group XI code at C69.0 to C69.6 (this tree's routed sites).

nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A stain or a gene result counts only as part of a histology report. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A tumour that overlaps two subsites with no stated origin takes the subsite for overlapping lesions (WHO coding Rule C): go back to the site step.

An HPV, p16 or Epstein-Barr virus result reported as a separate test does not change the code, except for a carcinoma of the oropharynx (go back and take the oropharynx option). A carcinoma that arose in a sinonasal papilloma is coded as the carcinoma named here.

nodes.question: What is in the file for this digestive tumour?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A tumour of the oesophagus and stomach together is recorded at the cardia (C16.0). A tumour of two digestive organs whose origin the report does not give, such as the stomach and small intestine, is recorded at overlapping lesion of the digestive system (C26.8). A report that names only the tissue beside an organ, such as peripancreatic tissue, does not name that organ: that tissue is the retroperitoneum (C48.0). If the site recorded does not follow these rules, go back to the site step. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Use the report's final diagnosis. An option that names an organ in brackets belongs to that organ: take it only when the site recorded is that organ. When the report gives two terms for one tumour and no single option covers both, choose the one with the higher code (WHO coding Rule K). A grade given together with a hormone type or with non-functioning records the grade, whose code is the higher: grade 1 is 8240, grade 2 or grade 3 is 8249, and the hormone types and non-functioning tumour are 8150 to 8156. When the report gives two grades, or the Ki-67 index and the mitotic count point to different grades, choose the higher grade. Bile duct carcinoma names a tumour type, not a site: keep the site the report states (WHO coding Rule H).

D1: the paediatric entities are the pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours and neuroendocrine carcinoma (Karges 2025), solid pseudopapillary neoplasm (Pfister 2022, p. 13; Stanley 2015; Ebrahim 2025), acinar cell carcinoma (Pfister 2022, p. 13), pancreatoblastoma (Group XII) and gastrointestinal stromal tumour (Group XII). The oesophageal, gastric, small-bowel and biliary carcinomas have no paediatric report (evidence data gap 1) and are picker entries. D5: the Rule K sentence on a grade with a hormone type is registrar question 8. Rule G: Nagtegaal 2020, Table 2 footnote, p. 4.

Evidence dg_not_malignant_gut and dg_not_malignant_pancreatobiliary, merged (departure 11).

nodes.question: Which carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: Type part of the name in the box and the matching options appear. The other names ICD-O-3.2 gives a tumour find it too. Use the report's own term. A carcinoma first diagnosed outside the digestive organs is coded at its primary site.

decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the pleura, heart and other thoracic sites (C38.0, C38.4-C39.9; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the pleura, heart or another thoracic site?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. Cytology of pleural or pericardial fluid, or of a needle aspirate, counts as cytology. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected cancer does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence pl_evidence and pl_cytology (departures 2 and 3 in the module docstring).

options.label: A referral letter or clinical note only - no imaging report, no tissue
An imaging report only - no tissue
A cytology report (pleural or pericardial fluid, or a needle aspirate) - no histology report
A histology report on a biopsy or resection, with or without immunohistochemistry or gene reports

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable
options.reason: A clinical note alone does not establish the tumour's type (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 5). It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3) at basis of diagnosis 1. ICCC-3 places that code at the pleura, the heart or another thoracic or respiratory site in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: The note says only possible or suspected
options.reason: Cancer is only possible on this evidence. Under the European registry rules a case that is only possibly cancer is not registered without pathology (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4).

A carcinoma in pleural or pericardial fluid that the file says began in another organ is a deposit: it is coded at that organ. Go back to the site step and record the organ the file names.

The hint's last sentences carry evidence pl_cytology option 0 (thoracic module departure 3).

options.label: Carcinoma, and the file does not name the organ where it began
options.reason: Recorded as Carcinoma, NOS (8010/3) at basis of diagnosis 5. A carcinoma whose site of origin is not known is recorded at C80.9, unknown primary site (WHO coding guidelines, ICD-O-3.1, printed p. 19). Cytology does not give the full histological type; a histology report confirms it.
options.coding_note: D8, D10. Evidence pl_cytology option 1 (topography_override C80.9, carried as a topography capture; app.js applies captures before finish()). ICCC-2017 range 136 places 8010/3 at C80.9 in XIf11.

Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D7: ICCC-2017 range 143 (XIIb) holds 8000-8005 at this tree's routed sites; the referral names the code (refer_code).

options.label: Suspicious for malignancy, atypical, indeterminate, or benign
options.reason: A cytology report that calls the tumour suspicious, atypical or indeterminate does not register it: it is only possible (Visser 2023, European Network of Cancer Registries, rule 4), and a benign result registers nothing.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and an imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology leaves imaging as the best evidence.

options.label: No malignant cells, scant material, or a non-diagnostic report - and no imaging report is in the file
options.coding_note: Non-diagnostic cytology and no imaging leave the note as the best evidence; Cytology stays on the case (Group 10's split).

nodes.question: What does the histology report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: Mesothelioma is coded in Group XII. A carcinoma in the pleura, pericardium or heart that began in another organ is a deposit: choose a deposit of a tumour that began elsewhere, and the case is coded at that organ.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence pl_histology (departures 4 to 8). Data gap 5: Sauter 2022 and the ICCR mesothelioma dataset name no primary carcinoma of the pleura, pericardium or heart, so the screen offers carcinoma with no type named, the picker and the deposit question.

options.label: Mesothelioma of any type: diffuse or localized, epithelioid, sarcomatoid, desmoplastic or biphasic
options.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes mesothelioma from Mesothelioma, malignant (9050/3) to Mesothelioma, biphasic, malignant (9053/3), and ICCC-3 places those codes in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence pl_histology option 0. Evidence conflicts, Group 12: mesothelioma is ICCC-2017 XIIa5 at every site. Sauter 2022, p. 2.

options.label: A malignant tumour the report does not type, with immunohistochemistry that compares mesothelioma and carcinoma

options.label: Leukaemia, or leukaemic infiltration

options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the pleura, the heart or another thoracic or respiratory site belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 places 8800-8921 and 9120-9133 in Group IX at the Group XI sites; a bone sarcoma arises in bone, which no Group XI tree routes.

options.label: Teratoma or another germ cell tumour

options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 range 101 (Xb2) places 9080-9084 at the extragonadal sites.

options.label: Another malignant tumour the report names that is not a carcinoma or melanoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 Group XII holds the specified malignant tumours no other group codes. Code the case from the Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) tree.

nodes.question: Which pattern does the immunohistochemistry report give?
nodes.hint: Mesothelial markers are calretinin, WT1, cytokeratin 5/6 and D2-40 (podoplanin). Carcinoma markers are claudin 4, MOC31, BG8 and BerEP4. Answer from the stains the report calls positive or negative.
nodes.coding_note: Evidence pl_ihc and ihc_rules 1-2, built as a choice (departure 7). The 8044/3 rule (thoracic SMARCA4-deficient undifferentiated tumour, Sauter 2022, p. 10) is not built: D4, registrar question 3.

options.label: Two or more mesothelial markers (calretinin, WT1, cytokeratin 5/6, D2-40) are positive, and the carcinoma markers (claudin 4, MOC31, BG8, BerEP4) are negative
options.reason: This is the mesothelioma pattern (ICCR mesothelioma dataset, 3rd edition, p. 12). ICD-O-3.2 codes mesothelioma from Mesothelioma, malignant (9050/3) to Mesothelioma, biphasic, malignant (9053/3), and ICCC-3 places those codes in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence ihc_rules 1 (pl_ihc), built as a choice (departure 7).

options.label: Claudin 4 is positive, or two or more of MOC31, BG8 and BerEP4 are positive, and the mesothelial markers are negative
options.coding_note: Evidence ihc_rules 2: 'carcinoma: the next question asks whether the report names the organ where it began' (departure 7; D10).

options.label: Neither pattern, or the report gives too few stains to decide
options.reason: The stains do not settle the tumour type. It is registered as Neoplasm, malignant (8000/3). ICCC-3 places that code at the pleura, the heart or another thoracic or respiratory site in Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms), not in Group XI. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: Evidence pl_ihc fallback (8000/3), a Group XII code at these sites: refer_code 8000 (D7; departure 7).

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the pleura, the heart or another thoracic or respiratory site are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. The five non-malignant lines of evidence pl_histology (departure 4).

decision_trees.tree_label: Carcinomas of the parathyroid and other endocrine glands (C75.0, C75.2, C75.4-C75.9; ICCC-3 Group XI, behaviour 3 only)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour of the parathyroid or another endocrine gland?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A parathyroidectomy or another resection report counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. An immunohistochemistry or gene report on its own does not stand in for a histology report. Serum calcium and parathyroid hormone results raise the question of parathyroid carcinoma and do not register it. A deposit of a cancer that began in another organ is coded at that organ: go back to the site step and record the organ the file names. A paraganglioma, a craniopharyngioma, a pituitary tumour or a pineal tumour is coded in its own group: go back and search its name. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: the evidence tiers; the router's site capture chose this tree. A tier a Lab Report can join routes through a laboratory screen when Lab Report is ticked (registrar, 6 October 2026). The checklist rules are in docs/evidence_documents/group_11.json. Evidence pt_evidence, en_evidence and pt_cytology (departures 1 to 5 in the module docstring).

options.label: A referral letter or clinical note only - no imaging report, no tissue
An imaging report (ultrasound, CT, MRI or a nuclear medicine scan) - no tissue
Cytology only - a fine-needle aspirate, a smear or a fluid sample; no histology report
A histology report: parathyroidectomy, biopsy or other resection, with or without immunohistochemistry or gene reports

nodes.question: What does the referral letter or clinical note say?
nodes.hint: No imaging report or tissue report is in the file. A note alone never establishes a carcinoma's type.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2, D7. Visser O, et al. Frontiers in Oncology 2023;13:1250549, rules 4 and 5, p. 03: 8000/3 at basis 1 when cancer is at least probable; 'possible' is not registrable. Evidence context 'referral': reached with evidence_tests [], which no option changes.

options.label: The note states a malignant tumour as the diagnosis, or as probable (not a craniopharyngioma or a paraganglioma, which Group III and Group IV code)

nodes.question: What is in the file for this tumour at the peritoneum or retroperitoneum, an ill-defined site, the brain or spinal cord, or with no primary site found?
nodes.hint: A radiology report counts as imaging. A pathology report on a biopsy or resection counts as histology. A biopsy or cytology report that calls the specimen inadequate or non-diagnostic counts as no tissue. An immunohistochemistry or gene report on its own does not stand in for a histology report. A deposit of a cancer that began in another organ is coded at that organ: go back to the site step and record the organ the file names. A squamous cell or basal cell carcinoma of a region, such as the arm, the chin or the forehead, is skin: go back to the site step and record the skin of that region. A primary tumour of the brain, spinal cord or meninges that is not a carcinoma is coded in Group III: go back and search its name. A report that calls the tumour possible or suspected does not register it.

nodes.question: Does the report call the tumour a deposit?
nodes.hint: A carcinoma in a lymph node or another organ is recorded at the organ where it began. Some tests point to an organ: Epstein-Barr virus encoded RNA (EBER) to the nasopharynx, p16 or high-risk human papillomavirus to the oropharynx, ultraviolet-signature mutations to the skin. Record that organ only when the report or the treating clinician names it as the primary site. A site written with a prefix such as peri- or para-, or as the area or region of a site, stays at the ill-defined site unless the tumour type shows its tissue.

nodes.question: What does the report call the tumour?
nodes.hint: When no primary site is found, a tumour name that ICD-O ties to one organ is recorded at that organ: papillary thyroid carcinoma at the thyroid, parathyroid carcinoma at the parathyroid gland, hepatocellular carcinoma at the liver, infiltrating duct carcinoma at the breast. First check that the report does not place the primary somewhere else. Tissue around the pancreas, the adrenal gland or the caecum is retroperitoneum (C48.0). A neuroblastoma, paraganglioma, sarcoma, germ cell tumour or lymphoma of the retroperitoneum is coded in its own group: go back and search its name. ICD-O ties high-grade and low-grade serous carcinoma to the ovary: record the peritoneum only when the report says the tumour began in the peritoneum. A carcinoma found in the brain, spinal cord or meninges is almost always a deposit: it is coded at the organ where it began, unless the report states that it began here.

options.coding_note: WHO Rule E (section 4.2.8): every leukaemia except myeloid sarcoma is C42.1, so the hop carries the marrow. A myeloid sarcoma option is not built: check_leukaemia_referrals_record_marrow admits a site-keeping Group I referral only on the nodes it lists.

options.label: A sarcoma
options.reason: A soft tissue sarcoma of the peritoneum, retroperitoneum, an ill-defined site or an unknown primary site belongs to ICCC-3 Group IX. Code the case from the Group IX (soft tissue sarcomas) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 places 8800-8921 and 9120-9133 in Group IX at the Group XI sites; a bone sarcoma arises in bone, which no Group XI tree routes.

options.label: Teratoma or another germ cell tumour
options.reason: Germ cell tumours, teratomas among them, belong to ICCC-3 Group X at the peritoneum, retroperitoneum, an ill-defined site or an unknown primary site. Code the case from the Group X (germ cell tumours) tree.
options.coding_note: ICCC-2017 range 101 (Xb2) places 9080-9084 at the extragonadal sites.

options.label: Another malignant tumour the report names that is not a carcinoma or melanoma
options.reason: ICCC-3 Group XII holds the specified malignant tumours no other group codes. Code the case from the Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) tree.

nodes.question: Which tumour does the report diagnose?
nodes.hint: These tumours of the peritoneum, retroperitoneum, an ill-defined site or an unknown primary site are benign, borderline or in situ, as ICD-O-3.2 prints them or as the report states them. ICCC-3 Group XI registers malignant tumours (behaviour 3) only, so none is recorded as a Group XI cancer.
nodes.coding_note: Contract §4.2: exclusions with the ICD-O-3.2 Preferred term at each (code, behaviour), read by excl() from icdo32.sqlite. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the stated behaviour decides; a pair ICD-O-3.2 does not print is admitted only through build_database.ICDO32_MATRIX_RULE. The two non-malignant lines of evidence pe_histology (departure 8).

options.label: Peritoneal inclusion cyst (also called multicystic or cystic mesothelioma)

behaviour_exclusion.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes a peritoneal inclusion cyst as Peritoneal inclusion cysts (9055/0), behaviour 0, benign. ICCC-3 Group XI registers behaviour 3 (malignant) only, so no Group XI code is recorded.

options.coding_note: Evidence pe_histology option 1.

options.label: Well-differentiated papillary mesothelioma (well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour) of the peritoneum

behaviour_exclusion.reason: ICD-O-3.2 codes a well-differentiated papillary mesothelial tumour of the peritoneum as Epithelioid mesothelioma, benign (9052/0), behaviour 0, benign. ICCC-3 Group XI registers behaviour 3 (malignant) only, so no Group XI code is recorded.

options.coding_note: Evidence pe_histology option 2.

options.label: Another tumour the report calls benign, borderline or in situ
options.reason: A tumour the report calls benign, borderline or in situ is not a malignant tumour. ICCC-3 Group XI registers behaviour 3 (malignant) only, so no Group XI code is recorded.
options.coding_note: Catch-all of the exclusion screen. Rule F (registrar, 8 October 2026, review A6): the report's stated behaviour decides.

nodes.question: Where does the report say the primary tumour is?
nodes.hint: The tumour in the peritoneum, retroperitoneum, an ill-defined site or an unknown primary site is a deposit, not a separate registration: the case is coded at its primary site. A melanoma is answered at the step before, from the melanoma option.
nodes.coding_note: D10, Group 10 n_deposit adapted. SELF_REFERRAL is True: build_database's check_refer_terminals fails a referral to Group XI from Group XI's own file.

options.coding_note: D10; WHO Rule E.

options.label: Another tumour, or a tumour of unstated type, whose primary has not been found
options.reason: A deposit with no identified primary, other than a carcinoma, belongs in ICCC-3 Group XII (other and unspecified malignant neoplasms) and is recorded at C80.9. Code the case from the Group XII tree.
options.coding_note: D10; WHO section 4.2.2: an unknown primary is C80.9, not the deposit's site.

nodes.question: Which carcinoma does the report name?
nodes.hint: Type part of the name in the box and the matching options appear. The other names ICD-O-3.2 gives a tumour find it too. Use the report's own term. A carcinoma first diagnosed outside an ill-defined or unknown site is coded at its primary site.
nodes.coding_note: D2 (registrar, 8 October 2026: 'Picker, as in Group 10'): every code ICCC-2017 places in Group XI (behaviour 3) at all of g11_unspecified's routed sites (C48.0-C48.8, C70.0-C72.9, C76.0-C76.8, C80.9), plus the standing-rule-3 codes the evidence names (D11: none); less the [obs] Preferred terms (D3: 8042, 8124, 8130, 8141, 8245, 8251, 8350, 8440, 8450, 8508, 8512, 8551, 8780), the XId melanoma codes the melanoma option reaches (D13) and the codes the histology screen and its subtype screens offer (8010); 175 options in code order. Valid at only some routed sites, so not offered: 8158, 8290.
